claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with a few basics:

1. **How many children are you asking about?** (Please provide their names or how you'd like to refer to them)

Once I know this, I'll ask about each child's circumstances to determine eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 16 and lives at home with you in the UK.

Since Alex is 16, his eligibility will depend on whether he's continuing in approved education or training. Let me ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he at school, college, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Alex being in college doing A-levels would qualify as approved education.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex working at all?** If yes, how many hours per week does he work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just focusing on his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for that information.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have the right to reside here?** (For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled/pre-settled status, or another immigration status?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. I'm a UK citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Does Alex receive any benefits in his own name?** (For example, Employment and Support Allowance, Universal Credit, or any other benefits?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I don't really know if he gets anything in his own name or not.

conversation.text:
## Good News! You appear to be **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Here's why:

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ **Alex is 16 and in approved education** - He's doing his A-levels at college, which counts as approved education. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training.

✓ **Alex lives at home with you** - You're responsible for him and he lives with you in the UK.

✓ **Alex is not working** - This is important because Child Benefit stops if a 16-17 year old works 24 hours or more per week and leaves education.

✓ **You're a UK citizen living in the UK** - You meet the residence requirements.

✓ **No disqualifying benefits likely** - While you're unsure if Alex receives any benefits in his own name, it's very unlikely for a 16-year-old student living at home and doing A-levels to be claiming benefits like Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance that would disqualify him.

### What to remember:

- Child Benefit can continue as long as Alex stays in approved education or training until he turns 20
- If Alex starts working 24 hours or more per week and leaves education, you'll need to notify HMRC
- If Alex starts claiming certain benefits in his own name (like Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance), this could affect eligibility

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If Alex's circumstances change, make sure to update HMRC.
